A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AVATAR study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original AVATAR benchmark evaluations, component ablations, training analyses and experiments with 7B and 3B models.

after.justification: v4 retains original AVATAR experiments and adds multimodal mathematics evaluations, additional video reasoning results and training diagnostics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 3–11 retain the same stratified replay, hinting, TAS weighting, rewards and VCRS procedure. Expanded explanations and newly specified helper-model sizes do not establish an algorithm change; the mathematics experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark coverage and adds Vision-R1-RL training with MathVerse, MathVista, MMK12 and R1-OneVision-Bench evaluation. It also evaluates Video-MMMU, VSI-Bench, SciVideoBench and Video-TT, substantially extending coverage into mathematical, spatial and scientific reasoning.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add GRPO-trained Ola-7B and Qwen2.5-Omni controls within the main comparisons, beyond v2's existing GRPO ablations. The new mathematics comparison includes OpenVLThinker-7B and VLAAThinker-VL-7B alongside Qwen2.5-VL and GRPO. Existing state-of-the-art comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce a Qwen2.5-VL-7B mathematics training configuration and measurements of advantage distributions and solvable-problem percentages over training. The retained video protocol, including 32 sampled frames, LoRA settings and staged reward configurations, is unchanged. Specifying teacher and judge sizes supplies previously missing detail rather than demonstrating changed settings.

E4.justification: v4 adds advantage-distribution and hinting-solvability analyses, mathematics component ablations and revised video component tests. It removes the 50,000-sample critical-step analysis, buffer-capacity sweep and earlier no-hinting benchmark row. The SFT ablation is retained as Table 7, and the loss-position, mixing-ratio, reward and model-scale analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 4 adds uncertainty margins to retained audio-visual component-ablation scores that had only point estimates in v2. Tables 2–3 retain 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, but v4 omits the earlier specification of 10,000 resamples and the percentile method. These reporting changes do not establish additional training runs.

E6.justification: Shared scores in Tables 2–3 and matched curriculum, SFT, reward and 3B tables are unchanged. v4 adds control and benchmark results, including MathVerse 49.6 versus GRPO's 48.1 and SciVideoBench 31.4 versus 30.3, plus advantage-distribution and solvability findings. Results from the deleted critical-step, buffer-capacity and earlier no-hinting analyses are removed.

T1.justification: The objectives, TAS function, reward definitions and VCRS formula in Equations 1–11 retain the same mathematics. No formal theorem, proof or derivation is added or removed. The attention-sink rationale and deleted critical-step study concern conceptual motivation and empirical evidence.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows its second contribution from broader reward-signaling and credit-assignment approaches to TAS positional weighting. The abstract and introduction explicitly quantify advantages over GRPO. The central replay-plus-TAS contribution, original headline benchmark gains and 5× sample-efficiency claim remain.

C2.justification: TAS motivation shifts from an SFT-derived critical-step distribution toward attention sinks and prevention of attention drift. Replay is explained as preserving rare successes and restoring group reward variance. New mathematics discussion attributes greater importance to TAS and hinting, while the buffer-capacity-specific diversity-versus-staleness discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies Qwen2.5-VL-72B as the hint generator and InternVL3-2B as the judge. Conversely, it removes the TAS implementation listing and GPT-4o critical-step annotation prompt. Algorithm 1, principal hyperparameters, hint and judge prompts, and the project link remain available in the PDFs.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantive contrasts with DAPO and prioritized experience replay, and motivates TAS through attention-sink research while removing GRPO-lambda and CAPO discussion. New mathematics and video evaluations add associated literature. Section 5.1 also recharacterizes TW-GRPO from statistical weighting to uniform credit, conflicting with v4's earlier variance-based characterization.

P1.justification: Substantial paragraph rewrites affect the introduction, TAS motivation and results discussion. The appendix becomes separately titled Supplementary Material, research questions are reordered, and the SFT analysis moves from the main text into the supplement. This constitutes extensive narrative revision beyond adding experiments.

P2.justification: v4 adds advantage-distribution and hinting plots plus mathematics and video benchmark tables, removes critical-step and buffer-capacity displays, and restructures Tables 2–4. The SFT table moves to the supplement. Tables 2–3 change highlighting from overall best/second-best scores to best scores within each RL block.

improvement.justification: Broader GRPO comparisons across both base models and new mathematics/video evaluations make AVATAR's incremental benefit and generality easier to assess while retaining the principal ablations. These gains are tempered by removal of critical-step validation, the buffer-capacity study and TAS code listing, reduced bootstrap detail, and an inconsistent characterization of TW-GRPO. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
